title: Feed the Children — WebAR Donation Experience
subtitle: XR · WebAR · Nonprofit
heroImageAlt: Feed the Children WebAR donation experience on three phones

overview.label: Story
overview.heading: Overview
overview.body: A web-based AR donation experience for Feed the Children, developed with the Truesense fundraising team. No app install — scanning a code opens the browser and places a shoppable classroom pantry in the donor's room.

problem.label: Problem
problem.heading: Why this needed to exist
problem.body: Donors give more when they can see who they're helping. Feed the Children needed an activation that turned abstract statistics — a dollar providing $9 of food and essentials — into something tangible, without an app-download barrier in front of the give-flow.

approach.label: Approach
approach.heading: How the work got done
approach.body: Built on 8th Wall WebAR: scanning a printed QR magnet opens a 3D classroom food pantry placed on any surface — stocked shelves, a real class roster with the kids' photos, and a hand-written 'Tap here to donate today' sign. Interactions mirror physical behavior: drag the kiosk to move it, open the cabinet doors, and tap the sign to hand off to the secure feedthechildren.org donation page.

outcomes.label: Outcomes
outcomes.heading: What changed once it shipped
outcomes.body: A full prototype journey from physical touchpoint → AR → donation page, keeping the donor inside one narrative: scan, meet the class, stock the pantry, give.

credits.label: Credits
credits.heading: One last thing
credits.body: Designed for Feed the Children with Truesense — a QR-triggered, browser-based AR pantry that turns a classroom shelf into a donation funnel.
